main_text.l: Ceu meruere, precor. Mitte damna, mitte clades Triste quae pectus premant: Malisque abominatus impios perde Illox vexet vbique Ultrix ira trementes. Illorum famam, quaesitaque nomina dele, Disjuncti toto funditus orbe ruant.

l.i: Auro qui rutilantia Puro templa prius, sordida nunc iacent? Qui mutata suum lamna decus nobile perdidit?
Sanctis quae penetralibus Gemmarum nituit copia, per vias Qui nunc spreta feris sub pedibus sternitur hostiū?

Obryso pretiosior Auro, cur soboles squallet Isacidum? Cur nunc terribili servitio subdita spernitur, Turpes quisquiliae velut, Aut effecta luto vascula ductili: Qua vilis figuli torta manu composuit rota?
Atqui immania parvulis Praebent monstra suis vbera foetibus:

page.notes: The ornamental strip between the upper verse and "Caput quartum." is a woodcut border, not text. Doubtful readings: "hostiū?" (the mark over the u may be a tilde or a stroke, read as hostium), "Isacidum" (the long s is printed as a letter resembling f, read as s). "tremen tes" is read as "trementes". The stanza breaks follow the visible indentation of the lines. The verse is set in italic type throughout.
